\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Majority}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.Majority
\section{Overview}

This chapter records exact Fourier coefficients, relations between Fourier levels,
and dimensional monotonicity and asymptotics for majority on an odd number of variables.
Boolean inputs are expressed as signs, with false encoded by $1$ and true by $-1$;
majority returns the sign held by more than half of the coordinates, so no tie occurs.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Limiting majority level weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majorityLimitWeight}
\leanok
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b003
}
For each $k\in\mathbb N$, define the real number
\[
 L_k=\begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\frac{4}{\pi k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2},& k\text{ odd},\\
 0,& k\text{ even}.
 \end{cases}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Majority takes values in the signs]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_isPmOne}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
For every $m\in\mathbb N$ and every $x\in\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$, the majority function, which
is $1$ when more than $m$ coordinates are false and $-1$ otherwise, takes a value in
$\{-1,1\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Oddness of the majority function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_isOddFunc}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.isOddFunc, BooleanAnalysis.majority}
\difficulty{5}
For every $m\in\mathbb N$, let $M_m$ be the majority function on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$, with
value $1$ when more than $m$ coordinates are false and $-1$ otherwise. For every
$x\in\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$, complementing every coordinate negates its value: $M_m(\lnot
x)=-M_m(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. The Fourier
weight of $f$ at level $k$ is nonnegative.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier weights above the dimension vanish]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_eq_zero_of_lt}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers with $n<k$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$.
The Fourier weight of $f$ at level $k$ is zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier sums grouped by degree]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_fourier_sq_eq_sum_weightLevel}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$. For each
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $\widehat f(S)$ be the Fourier–Walsh coefficient of
$f$, and let $W_k[f]$ be its Fourier weight at level $k$. Then
$\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}g(|S|)\widehat f(S)^2=\sum_{k=0}^{n}g(k)W_k[f]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Stability as a sum of Fourier weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability_eq_sum_weightLevel}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_fourier_sq_eq_sum_weightLevel, BooleanAnalysis.stability_formula, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let
$f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. The noise stability at parameter $\rho$ is the
generating sum of the Fourier weights by level:
$$\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(f)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\rho^k W_k[f],$$ where
$W_k[f]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n],\,|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in
$\{-1,1\}$. If $W_k[f]$ denotes the sum of the squares of the Fourier--Walsh
coefficients over all subsets of $[n]$ of size $k$, then $\sum_{k=0}^{n} W_k[f]=1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Prefix domination for geometric weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_pow_mul_le_of_prefix_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $N\ge 0$, let $0\le\rho\le1$, and let $a,b:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$. Suppose that for
every integer $j$ with $0\le j\le N$, $\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}b(k)\le\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}a(k)$, and
that $\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b(k)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a(k)$, with an empty sum interpreted as zero.
Then $\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\rho^k b(k)\le\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\rho^k a(k)$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$ and let $S\subseteq[2m+1]$ have even cardinality. For the majority
function on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$, whose value is $1$ when more than $m$ coordinates are
false and $-1$ otherwise, the Fourier--Walsh coefficient at $S$ is zero: $\widehat
M_m(S)=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact odd majority coefficients]

Let $m\in\mathbb N$ and let $S\subseteq[2m+1]$ have odd cardinality. Set $r=(|S|-1)/2$,
where the quotient is an integer. For the majority function on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$, whose
value is $1$ when more than $m$ coordinates are false and $-1$ otherwise, its
Fourier--Walsh coefficient at $S$ is
\[\widehat M_m(S)=(-1)^r\frac{\binom{m}{r}}{\binom{2m}{2r}}\frac{\binom{2m}{m}}{2^{2m}}.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetry of binomial ratios]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.choose_div_choose_symm}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $m,p,q$ satisfying $p+q=m$, the following identity holds in the real
numbers: $\binom mq/\binom{2m}{2q}=\binom mp/\binom{2m}{2p}$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{5}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$ and let $S,T\subseteq[2m+1]$ satisfy $|S|+|T|=2m+2$. For the
majority function on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$, whose value is $1$ when more than $m$ coordinates
are false and $-1$ otherwise, the Fourier--Walsh coefficients satisfy $\widehat
M_m(S)=(-1)^m\widehat M_m(T)$.
\end{theorem}

  {BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_fourierCoeff_even}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p121-b006,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b004}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m,k\in\mathbb N$ and suppose $k$ is even. The Fourier weight at level $k$ of the
majority function on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$ is zero: $W_k[M_m]=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Odd-level Fourier weight of majority]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_odd}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b001}
\difficulty{5}
For $m,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k$ odd, let $M_m$ be the majority function on
$\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$ that is $1$ when more than $m$ coordinates are false and $-1$
otherwise. Its Fourier weight at level $k$ is $\displaystyle
W_k[M_m]=\binom{2m+1}{k}\left(\frac{\binom{m}{(k-1)/2}}{\binom{2m}{k-1}}\cdot\frac{\binom{2m}{m}}{2^{2m}}\right)^2$,
with the quotient interpreted as real division, including when its denominator is zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Duality of majority level weights]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weight_duality}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.choose_div_choose_symm, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_even, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_odd, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_eq_zero_of_lt, BooleanAnalysis.majority, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b004}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for every
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(M_m)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_m(S)^2$.
For every $k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\le2m+1$,
\[
 W_{2m+2-k}(M_m)=\frac{k}{2m+2-k}W_k(M_m).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Two-step binomial identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.choose_add_two_mul}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $N,k,a$ be natural numbers with $N=k+a$. Then
$\binom{N+2}{k}(a+2)(a+1)=\binom{N}{k}(N+2)(N+1)$.
\end{lemma}

For natural numbers $m$ and $k$, if $k$ is odd and $k\le 2m+1$, then the Fourier weight
at level $k$ of majority on the Boolean hypercube of dimension $2m+3$ is strictly less
than that of majority on the Boolean hypercube of dimension $2m+1$.
\end{theorem}

  {BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majorityLimitWeight}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b002}
For every odd natural number $k$, let $L_k=\frac{4}{\pi k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}$. The
level-$k$ Fourier weight of majority on the Boolean cube of dimension $2m+1$ converges
to $L_k$ as $m$ tends to infinity. Moreover, for every natural number $m$ with $k\le
(2m+1)/2$, where the quotient is rounded down, its level-$k$ Fourier weight lies between
$L_k$ and $\left(1+\frac{2k}{2m+1}\right)L_k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Cumulative majority Fourier weight comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_prefix_weight_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weightLevel_even, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weight_strictAnti, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_weightLevel_eq_one, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_eq_zero_of_lt, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.majority, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$. For every $j\in\mathbb N$ with $j\leq2(m+1)+2$, the cumulative
Fourier weight through levels below $j$ of majority on $\{0,1\}^{2(m+1)+1}$ is at most
that of majority on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$:
\[\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}W_k[M_{m+1}]\leq\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}W_k[M_m],\]
where $W_k[f]$ is the sum of squared Fourier--Walsh coefficients over subsets of size
$k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of majority noise stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_noiseStability_antitone}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_prefix_weight_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability_eq_sum_weightLevel, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_pow_mul_le_of_prefix_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sum_weightLevel_eq_one, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.weightLevel_eq_zero_of_lt, BooleanAnalysis.majority, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0\leq\rho\leq1$, and let $m\in\mathbb N$. For a Boolean
function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, define its noise stability by
$\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(f)=\langle f,T_{\rho}f\rangle$, where
$T_{\rho}f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x)$ and the inner
product and Fourier coefficients use the uniform measure. Then the majority functions on
the two respective odd-dimensional cubes satisfy
$\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(M_{m+1})\leq\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(M_m)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform majority spectral asymptotics]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.majority_weight_asymptotics}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove, BooleanAnalysis.majority, BooleanAnalysis.weightLevel}

There is a constant $C\ge 0$ such that, for all natural numbers $m$ and $k$ with $k$
odd, $k>0$, and $2k^2\le 2m+1$, the majority function on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$ has Fourier
weight $W_k$ at level $k$ and Fourier weight $W_{>k}$ on levels strictly greater than
$k$ satisfying
\[
\left|\frac{W_k}{(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-3/2}}-1\right|\le \frac{C}{k},\qquad
\left|\frac{W_{>k}}{(2/\pi)^{3/2}k^{-1/2}}-1\right|\le \frac{C}{k}.
\]
\end{theorem}
